_meta.scope: Effect of keeping vs closing Spanish nuclear plants on wholesale price (pool, EUR/MWh) and household bill. Evidence base for 'La factura en juego | Elecciones 29N'.
_meta.method_note: Only figures found in the cited sources. Where a value is derived by us (e.g. % converted to EUR/MWh, EUR/MWh converted to EUR/household/year) it is flagged 'derived'.

inside_2027_2030.key_fact: After Orden TED/864/2026 NO reactor closes in 2027, 2028 or 2029. All four 2027-2030 closures are concentrated in Jun-Nov 2030 (>4,000 MW in under 6 months, AleaSoft 18/08/2026).

calendar_summary.implication_for_model: During 2027-2029 the fleet runs fully under BOTH the PSOE calendar and the PP/Vox derogation, so the price difference between programmes is ~0 in those years; it appears only from mid-2030 (Almaraz) / Q4 2030 (Ascó I, Cofrentes) and becomes structural 2031-2035.

price_impact_studies.source: PwC - 'Precio de la electricidad y energía nuclear: ¿Cómo impacta el parque nuclear en el precio de la electricidad?' (static, no-nuclear today)
price_impact_studies.funded_by: PwC; commissioner not disclosed in sources found. Disseminated by Foro Nuclear (industry association); author partner Óscar Barrero published it on Endesa's corporate blog. Treat as INDUSTRY-ALIGNED. Called 'sesgo deliberado' by energias-renovables.com (17/08/2026).
price_impact_studies.scenario: Whole fleet (7.4 GW) absent in current system; CCGT replaces almost all lost output
price_impact_studies.period: Counterfactual on 2024 market (Civismo cites +36.8 EUR/MWh 'si el cierre ya se hubiera producido en 2024')
price_impact_studies.notes: +23% bill for domestic and SMEs, +35% industry; ~8,000 MEUR/yr consumer saving; +21 MtCO2/yr.

price_impact_studies.source: PwC - same report, forward-looking PNIEC scenario
price_impact_studies.scenario: Full closure per calendar, even with PNIEC targets met
price_impact_studies.period: 'a futuro' (post-closure horizon, ~2035). An earlier PwC paper (contexto-nuclear-espana.pdf, 2024) gives 13.26 EUR/MWh for accelerated closure.
price_impact_studies.notes: This 13 EUR/MWh figure is the one quoted by the PP in its Senate motion (Nov 2025).

price_impact_studies.scenario: Closure of national + Catalan fleet vs 10-year extension
price_impact_studies.notes: Extending national and Catalan fleet 10 years saves at least 5,400 MEUR on Catalonia's electricity bill (figure used by Feijóo, Apr 2026).

price_impact_studies.scenario: Almaraz (2.1 GW) closed in 2025, gas price shock from Middle East conflict; CCGT replacement
price_impact_studies.period: 2025 counterfactual; also +22 EUR/MWh for whole fleet absent in a similar gas-crisis scenario projected to 2035
price_impact_studies.notes: +24% bill households/small firms, +35% industry; ~8,800 MEUR/yr; ~144 EUR/yr per average domestic consumer. Stress-case only; 47 EUR/MWh for 2 GW is not consistent with 37 EUR/MWh for 7.4 GW unless gas price assumptions differ strongly.

price_impact_studies.source: Monitor Deloitte - 'La contribución de la energía nuclear a la competitividad industrial en España' (presented at CEOE)
price_impact_studies.funded_by: Commissioner not disclosed in sources found; presented 15/01/2026 at CEOE with Foro Nuclear president on panel. Treat as INDUSTRY-ALIGNED.
price_impact_studies.scenario: Extension of whole fleet beyond 2035 calendar vs closure
price_impact_studies.notes: 1,400 MEUR/yr saving for industry; -14 MtCO2/yr in 2035.

price_impact_studies.source: Natalia Fabra (UC3M / EnergyEconLab), 'The Price and Emissions Effects of Extending Nuclear Lifetimes: Evidence from Spain' (CEPR DP21053; SERIEs 2026)
price_impact_studies.funded_by: ERC Advanced Grant ENERGY-IN-TRANSITION (EU public research funding). Author is a board member of Red Eléctrica (Redeia) and Government adviser (elEconomista) - flag potential perceived alignment with Government.
price_impact_studies.scenario: Almaraz extension to 2030 vs closure 2027-28; static (investment unchanged) vs dynamic (renewables/storage shortfall)
price_impact_studies.impact_eur_mwh: Reported in %: static extension LOWERS wholesale prices 4-8% (PNIEC baseline) or 5-11% (Feasible baseline) in 2028-2031. With 25% investment shortfall extension RAISES prices +4.5-7.2% (PNIEC) / +1.6-2.4% (Feasible) in 2028-30 and ~+10-11% in 2031; with 50% shortfall +15-20% pre-2031, up to +46.8% beyond 2031. Derived at a 60 EUR/MWh pool: static ~2.4-6.6 EUR/MWh lower with extension; dynamic 25% case ~1-4 EUR/MWh higher 2028-30, ~6 EUR/MWh higher 2031.
price_impact_studies.notes: Peer-reviewed academic. Static effect consistent in sign with industry studies; dynamic result reverses sign. Investment response is not empirically pinned down (author's caveat).

price_impact_studies.source: URJC Cátedra de Transición Energética (Eloy Sanz) + UPC (Víctor García Carrasco), 'Cierre nuclear y transición energética: el caso de Almaraz'
price_impact_studies.funded_by: COMMISSIONED BY GREENPEACE (anti-nuclear NGO). Flag as advocacy-funded.
price_impact_studies.scenario: Almaraz extension to 2030 vs closure per 2019 calendar; hourly simulations 2026-2033 with investment response
price_impact_studies.impact_eur_mwh: Extension: transitory price relief 2028-2030 (not quantified in coverage), then +5.5 EUR/MWh in 2033 (63.5 vs 58 EUR/MWh, +9.5%)
price_impact_studies.notes: Cumulative bill overcost of extension up to 3,831 MEUR to 2033; renewable coverage 2030 falls 65.8% -> 59.3%; up to 26,130 MEUR lost renewable/storage investment; +5.8-12.3 MtCO2. Renewables cover 96.4% of Almaraz output after closure.

price_impact_studies.source: MITECO - Orden TED/864/2026 (sensitivity analysis on PNIEC)
price_impact_studies.scenario: Almaraz extension to June 2030 vs PNIEC scenario
price_impact_studies.notes: -7% CCGT generation and -1.4% renewable generation in 2030 vs PNIEC. Extension 'contribuye de manera coyuntural a moderar la exposición ... a picos de precios' of gas. Enresa: no extra waste costs passed to consumers or budget.

price_impact_studies.source: MITECO / PNIEC 2023-2030 impact analysis, as stated by Minister Sara Aagesen (EFE interview)
price_impact_studies.scenario: PNIEC target scenario including nuclear closure calendar
price_impact_studies.impact_eur_mwh: No delta published; projected pool level 'inferiores a 40 EUR/MWh incluso con el cierre del parque nuclear'
price_impact_studies.notes: Government position: closure does not drive prices up. Fedea (Rodríguez, Sept 2025) and NERA/Fedea (Jan 2026) consider PNIEC wind and storage targets unattainable, which undermines this level.

price_impact_studies.source: Fedea - Diego Rodríguez, 'Sobre el cierre de la central nuclear de Almaraz'
price_impact_studies.funded_by: Fedea (think tank funded by large Spanish companies incl. banks and utilities - not verified in this research; flag as unverified)
price_impact_studies.scenario: Almaraz closure 2027-28 vs delay, realistic (non-PNIEC) 2030 system
price_impact_studies.impact_eur_mwh: Not quantified in the summary; concludes closure raises supply costs and emissions (more CCGT than PNIEC assumes)
price_impact_studies.notes: Recommends at least delaying the 2019 calendar. Replacing nuclear tax with charges would raise domestic bills ~1%.

price_impact_studies.scenario: Theoretical ceiling: Almaraz 2025 net output (14,752 GWh) fully replaced by CCGT
price_impact_studies.impact_eur_mwh: Not a pool delta. CCGT fuel+CO2 cost 139-153 EUR/MWh at gas 60 EUR/MWh and CO2 82 EUR/t; 27-30 TWh extra gas, 1,620-1,800 MEUR/yr
price_impact_studies.notes: Explicitly an upper bound, not a forecast. Also flags extension raises curtailment risk.

price_impact_studies.impact_eur_mwh: Not quantified in EUR/MWh in coverage
price_impact_studies.notes: Extension could raise wind and solar curtailment by ~40% in 2030.

price_impact_studies.source: OBS Business School - 'El sector energético en España, hacia una descarbonización sostenible'
price_impact_studies.notes: LOW RELIABILITY: claims +23% households/SMEs, +35% industry and 150-250 EUR/yr per household for Almaraz I alone - same percentages PwC gives for the WHOLE fleet. Do not use as input.

household_eur_per_year.value: ~144 EUR/yr per average domestic consumer for +47 EUR/MWh
household_eur_per_year.notes: Implies ~3.06 EUR/yr per household per 1 EUR/MWh (derived).

household_eur_per_year.value: Extension = up to 3,831 MEUR cumulative overcost on household+SME bills to 2033 (no per-household figure)

1 EUR/MWh on pool ~= 3.0-3.6 EUR/yr per household before taxes (consumption 250-300 kWh/month = 3.0-3.6 MWh/yr per eniplenitude.es); add IEE 5.11% and IVA 21% for final bill. PwC's 144 EUR / 47 EUR/MWh cross-checks at ~3.06.

range_eur_mwh.definition: Pool price effect of KEEPING the whole fleet (7.4 GW) operating vs closing per calendar, structural years 2031-2035. Positive = keeping lowers the pool (household saves). Not applicable to 2027-2029 (no closures in either scenario).
range_eur_mwh.stress_gas_crisis: 22-37 (PwC: +22 EUR/MWh in 2035 gas-crisis scenario; +37 EUR/MWh static counterfactual on 2024 market)
range_eur_mwh.per_gw_static_eur_mwh: ~1.2-2.0 EUR/MWh per GW kept (derived: PwC 13 / 7.4 GW = 1.8; Deloitte 14-15 / 7.4 GW = 1.9-2.0; Fabra static Almaraz 2.4-6.6 / 2.09 GW = 1.1-3.2)
range_eur_mwh.method: LOW = URJC/UPC (Greenpeace-funded) 2033 result scaled as-is (+5.5 EUR/MWh HIGHER price if Almaraz is kept, via crowded-out renewables) - the dynamic case where keeping costs money; Fabra's 25%-shortfall case gives the same sign (~+6 EUR/MWh in 2031). HIGH = industry-aligned forward estimates with PNIEC renewables (PwC 13, Deloitte 14-15 EUR/MWh in 2035). CENTRAL = our judgement: midpoint of Fabra's static Almaraz effect scaled to the full fleet (~1.4 EUR/MWh/GW x 7.4 GW = ~10) haircut by ~1/3 for partial investment crowding-out reported by Fabra and Aurora, ~= 6.5 EUR/MWh; also ~half of the industry PNIEC figure. Government (PNIEC) publishes no delta and says pool <40 EUR/MWh even with closure, consistent with the low end. Stress case shown separately; do not use as base.
range_eur_mwh.household_translation_central: 6.5 EUR/MWh x ~3.3 MWh/yr ~= 21 EUR/yr pre-tax (~27 EUR/yr incl. IEE+IVA) per household in 2031-2035 (derived). Range: approx -18 to +50 EUR/yr pre-tax.

caveats: With Almaraz extended to 8 June 2030, no reactor closes in 2027-2029; the PSOE vs PP/Vox difference in the 2027-2030 legislature is limited to H2 2030 (Almaraz from June, Ascó I from October, Cofrentes from December). Bill effects of 'derogating the calendar' are essentially a 2031-2035 (next-next legislature) story.

Ascó II (licence to 2031-10-01) and Vandellòs II (licence to 2030-07-26) need licence renewals even to reach the calendar dates; owners must request them, so 'keeping' also depends on utilities' economics (nuclear tax, Enresa fee ~11 EUR/MWh), not only on law.

Studies with large pro-nuclear effects (PwC, Deloitte) are industry-aligned and mostly static (replacement by CCGT); studies with negative effects (URJC/UPC) are Greenpeace-commissioned and rely on assumed investment crowding-out. The only independent academic study (Fabra, ERC-funded) shows both signs depending on the investment response.
Most estimates concern Almaraz (2.1 GW) only; scaling linearly to 7.4 GW is an approximation and ignores the dynamic effects.
Results depend heavily on gas and CO2 prices: PwC gas-crisis numbers (47 EUR/MWh for Almaraz, 22 EUR/MWh in 2035) are stress cases.
Percent results (Fabra, URJC) were converted to EUR/MWh using a ~58-60 EUR/MWh pool level; conversions are ours (derived).
Government (MITECO/PNIEC) never published a quantified pool delta for closure vs keeping; only a price level (<40 EUR/MWh) and generation shares.
Fedea's funding structure and the commissioner of the PwC and Deloitte reports were not verified in sources; flagged accordingly.
Household conversion uses 3.0-3.6 MWh/yr consumption; actual pass-through depends on tariff (PVPC passes pool immediately; fixed-price free-market contracts pass it with lag).
